content.value_statement: Teams often write implementation before clear behavioral tests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through strict Red-Green-Refactor cycles.
actual_capabilities: Guides users to write a failing test before production code.
Explains the Red-Green-Refactor workflow with simple TypeScript examples.
Provides checklist prompts for test writing, passing implementation, and refactoring.
Recommends behavior-focused test names using a clear naming pattern.
Highlights common TDD mistakes such as testing implementation details.
Shows incremental feature development through a slugify example.
limitations: Does not run tests or inspect project files by itself.
Does not provide framework-specific setup for every language or test runner.
Uses general TypeScript examples instead of full production architecture guidance.
Requires the user to supply requirements, existing code, and test commands.

use_cases.title: Start a New Feature
use_cases.description: Break a feature into small behaviors, write the first failing test, and implement only enough code to pass.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Discipline
use_cases.description: Use checklists to keep implementation, test naming, and refactoring aligned with TDD rules.

use_cases.title: Coach TDD Practice
use_cases.description: Teach developers how to move from simple tests to generalized implementation without large jumps.

prompt_templates.title: Write the First Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start this feature with TDD. Ask for the simplest behavior, then write only the first failing test.

prompt_templates.title: Move From Red to Green
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer has a failing test and needs minimal implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this failing test and error output. Suggest the smallest implementation change that should make it pass.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the Next Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer has one passing test and needs the next increment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this passing test and implementation. Propose the next behavior test that forces useful generalization.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor While Green
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after a complete green test run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these green tests and implementation, identify a small refactor that preserves behavior and improves design.

output_examples.input: I need a slugify helper, but I want to use TDD.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for the simplest expected behavior, drafts a failing lowercase test, and waits before implementation.

output_examples.input: My test passes after hardcoding the result. What next?
output_examples.output: The skill recommends adding a second test with different input to force a general implementation.

output_examples.input: All tests pass, and the implementation is duplicated.
output_examples.output: The skill checks that the suite is green, then suggests a small refactor while keeping behavior unchanged.

best_practices: Keep each cycle small enough to understand the failing reason clearly.
Name tests by observable behavior and the condition being tested.
Refactor only after all relevant tests are passing.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before a failing test exists.
Adding many tests before making the first one pass.
Testing private implementation details instead of visible behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill execute my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. The user or host agent must run project commands.

faq.question: Can I use it with languages other than TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are TypeScript, but the Red-Green-Refactor workflow applies across languages.

faq.question: Does hardcoding violate good design?
faq.answer: Temporary hardcoding can be acceptable during the green step when the next test forces generalization.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, expected behavior, existing test framework, and any relevant error output.

faq.question: Will it write complete production features?
faq.answer: It focuses on incremental tests and minimal implementation, not broad feature delivery in one step.

faq.question: Is this safe for existing codebases?
faq.answer: Yes, as guidance. Review all generated tests and code before applying changes to important branches.
